topic: Reactance, impedance and resonance (G5A; 12 pool questions)

notes.front: What is reactance?
notes.back: Opposition to the flow of alternating current caused by capacitance or inductance, measured in ohms, symbol X.
notes.explanation: Unlike resistance, reactance only opposes AC, and how strongly it opposes depends on frequency.
notes.example: A capacitor passes DC not at all but lets a fast AC signal through fairly easily; that frequency-dependent opposition is reactance.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G5A02, G5A09, G5A11

notes.front: What is inductive reactance?
notes.back: The opposition an inductor offers to AC, symbol XL, in ohms; it rises as frequency rises.
notes.explanation: A changing current in an inductor builds a magnetic field that opposes the change, and that opposition grows the faster the current changes.
notes.example: A choke that barely affects 60 Hz mains hum strongly opposes a 7 MHz radio signal.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G5A03, G5A05; US Navy NEETS Module 2 glossary: "The opposition to the flow of an alternating current caused by the inductance of a circuit, expressed in ohms. Identified by the letter XL."

notes.front: What is capacitive reactance?
notes.back: The opposition a capacitor offers to AC, symbol XC, in ohms; it falls as frequency rises.
notes.explanation: A capacitor charges and discharges each cycle; the faster the AC alternates, the less time it spends fighting the charge, so its opposition drops.
notes.example: A capacitor that almost blocks 60 Hz mains hum passes a 7 MHz radio signal with little opposition.
notes.source: NCVEC 2023–2027 General Pool, G5A04, G5A06; US Navy NEETS Module 2 glossary: "The opposition offered to the flow of an alternating current by capacitance, expressed in ohms. The symbol for capacitive reactance is Xc."

notes.front: What is admittance?
notes.back: The inverse of impedance: a measure of how easily a circuit lets AC current through.
notes.explanation: High impedance means the circuit resists current, so its admittance is low, and vice versa.
notes.example: Like conductance (1/resistance) but for AC circuits that include reactance as well as resistance.

notes.front: What is impedance matching?
notes.back: Adjusting a circuit so its impedance matches another's, so power transfers efficiently between them.
notes.explanation: A transformer, a pi-network or a matched length of transmission line can all be used to do this at radio frequencies.
notes.example: Matching a transmitter's 50-ohm output to an antenna's different feed-point impedance with a transformer, a pi-network, or a matched length of transmission line.

notes.front: What is a pi-network?
notes.back: One of the devices that can be used for impedance matching at radio frequencies.
notes.explanation: It is one of the standard ways to match impedances at radio frequencies, alongside a transformer or a matched feed line.
notes.example: Matching a transmitter's output stage to a 50-ohm antenna feed line, alongside a transformer or matched transmission line.

notes.front: What is an LC circuit?
notes.back: A circuit built from an inductor (L) and a capacitor (C), whose reactances interact to set a resonant frequency.
notes.explanation: Wired in series or parallel, an LC circuit is a resonant (tank) circuit: it stores energy alternately in the inductor and the capacitor at its resonant frequency.
notes.example: A series LC circuit's impedance is lowest at resonance; a parallel LC circuit's impedance is highest at resonance.
notes.source: US Navy NEETS Module 9: "A RESONANT CIRCUIT is often called a TANK CIRCUIT... IN A SERIES-LC CIRCUIT impedance is minimum and current is maximum... IN A PARALLEL-LC CIRCUIT impedance is maximum and current is minimum."

notes.front: What unit and letter symbol are used for reactance?
notes.back: The ohm; symbol X.
notes.explanation: Reactance is measured in the same unit as resistance because both oppose current, but only reactance depends on frequency.

notes.front: As the frequency of the applied AC rises, inductive reactance {{c1::increases}}.
notes.explanation: A faster-changing current builds a faster-changing magnetic field, and the inductor opposes that change more strongly.

notes.front: As the frequency of the applied AC rises, capacitive reactance {{c1::decreases}}.
notes.explanation: A capacitor spends less time fighting the charge each cycle as the AC alternates faster, so it opposes current less.

notes.front: How is impedance defined in an AC circuit?
notes.back: The ratio of voltage to current.
notes.explanation: It generalises Ohm's law to AC circuits, combining resistance and reactance into a single opposition to current.

notes.front: The reciprocal (inverse) of impedance is called {{c1::admittance}}.
notes.explanation: It is the AC-circuit equivalent of turning resistance into conductance.

notes.front: What happens to impedance in a series LC circuit at resonance?
notes.back: It becomes very low, because inductive and capacitive reactance cancel.
notes.explanation: At the resonant frequency XL and XC are equal and opposite, so only any resistance in the circuit is left to oppose current.

notes.front: What three devices can be used for impedance matching at radio frequencies?
notes.back: A transformer, a pi-network, or a matched length of transmission line.
notes.explanation: All three reshape how a circuit presents its impedance, without changing the frequency or the signal itself.

notes.front: What happens when inductive and capacitive reactance are equal in a series LC circuit?
notes.back: Resonance causes impedance to be very low
notes.choices:
A) Resonance causes impedance to be very high
B) Impedance is equal to the geometric mean of the inductance and capacitance
C) Resonance causes impedance to be very low
D) Impedance is equal to the arithmetic mean of the inductance and capacitance
notes.choicesExplained: A: resonance makes series LC impedance very low, not high. B: impedance at resonance is not a geometric mean of L and C. D: impedance at resonance is not an arithmetic mean of L and C either.
notes.explanation: When XL and XC are equal, they cancel, leaving only any resistance to oppose current, so the series impedance drops very low.

notes.front: What is reactance?
notes.back: Opposition to the flow of alternating current caused by capacitance or inductance
notes.choices:
A) Opposition to the flow of direct current caused by resistance
B) Opposition to the flow of alternating current caused by capacitance or inductance
C) Reinforcement of the flow of direct current caused by resistance
D) Reinforcement of the flow of alternating current caused by capacitance or inductance
notes.choicesExplained: A: that describes resistance opposing DC, not reactance opposing AC. C: resistance opposes current; it never reinforces it. D: reactance opposes AC, it does not reinforce it.
notes.explanation: Reactance is the frequency-dependent opposition capacitors and inductors offer to alternating current, distinct from resistance.

notes.front: Which of the following is opposition to the flow of alternating current in an inductor?
notes.back: Reactance
notes.choices:
A) Conductance
B) Reluctance
C) Admittance
D) Reactance
notes.choicesExplained: A: conductance is the reciprocal of DC resistance, not AC opposition. B: reluctance opposes magnetic flux in a magnetic circuit, not current. C: admittance is the inverse of impedance, not the opposition itself.
notes.explanation: An inductor opposes AC current through inductive reactance.

notes.front: Which of the following is opposition to the flow of alternating current in a capacitor?
notes.back: Reactance
notes.choices:
A) Conductance
B) Reluctance
C) Reactance
D) Admittance
notes.choicesExplained: A: conductance is the reciprocal of DC resistance. B: reluctance concerns magnetic circuits, not capacitors. D: admittance is the inverse of impedance, not the opposition itself.
notes.explanation: A capacitor opposes AC current through capacitive reactance.

notes.front: How does an inductor react to AC?
notes.back: As the frequency of the applied AC increases, the reactance increases
notes.choices:
A) As the frequency of the applied AC increases, the reactance decreases
B) As the amplitude of the applied AC increases, the reactance increases
C) As the amplitude of the applied AC increases, the reactance decreases
D) As the frequency of the applied AC increases, the reactance increases
notes.choicesExplained: A: that is how capacitive, not inductive, reactance behaves. B and C: inductive reactance depends on frequency, not on the signal's amplitude.
notes.explanation: A faster-changing AC current makes an inductor's opposing magnetic field change faster too, raising its reactance.

notes.front: How does a capacitor react to AC?
notes.back: As the frequency of the applied AC increases, the reactance decreases
notes.choices:
A) As the frequency of the applied AC increases, the reactance decreases
B) As the frequency of the applied AC increases, the reactance increases
C) As the amplitude of the applied AC increases, the reactance increases
D) As the amplitude of the applied AC increases, the reactance decreases
notes.choicesExplained: B: that is how inductive, not capacitive, reactance behaves. C and D: capacitive reactance depends on frequency, not on the signal's amplitude.
notes.explanation: A capacitor spends less time fighting the charge each cycle as the AC alternates faster, so its reactance falls.

notes.front: What is the term for the inverse of impedance?
notes.back: Admittance
notes.choices:
A) Conductance
B) Susceptance
C) Reluctance
D) Admittance
notes.choicesExplained: A: conductance is the inverse of resistance only, not of the whole impedance. B: susceptance is only the reactive part of admittance, not the whole inverse. C: reluctance belongs to magnetic circuits, not to impedance.
notes.explanation: Admittance is the complete reciprocal of impedance, combining conductance and susceptance.

notes.front: What is impedance?
notes.back: The ratio of voltage to current
notes.choices:
A) The ratio of current to voltage
B) The product of current and voltage
C) The ratio of voltage to current
D) The product of current and reactance
notes.choicesExplained: A: current divided by voltage is admittance, the inverse of impedance. B: impedance is a ratio, not a product. D: impedance is voltage divided by current, not current times reactance.
notes.explanation: Impedance generalises Ohm's law to AC circuits as the ratio of voltage to current.

notes.front: What unit is used to measure reactance?
notes.back: Ohm
notes.choices:
A) Farad
B) Ohm
C) Ampere
D) Siemens
notes.choicesExplained: A: the farad measures capacitance, not reactance. C: the ampere measures current. D: the siemens measures admittance or conductance, the inverse quantity.
notes.explanation: Reactance opposes current the same way resistance does, so it shares its unit, the ohm.

notes.front: Which of the following devices can be used for impedance matching at radio frequencies?
notes.back: All these choices are correct
notes.choices:
A) A transformer
B) A Pi-network
C) A length of transmission line
D) All these choices are correct
notes.choicesExplained: A, B and C are each true on their own, but each names only one of the three matching methods, so the complete answer is D.
notes.explanation: A transformer, a pi-network and a correctly matched length of transmission line can all be used to match impedances at RF.

notes.front: What letter is used to represent reactance?
notes.back: X
notes.choices:
A) Z
B) X
C) B
D) Y
notes.choicesExplained: A: Z is the symbol for impedance. C: B is the symbol for susceptance. D: Y is the symbol for admittance.
notes.explanation: Reactance is given the letter X, to distinguish it from impedance (Z) and resistance (R).

notes.front: What occurs in an LC circuit at resonance?
notes.back: Inductive reactance and capacitive reactance cancel
notes.choices:
A) Current and voltage are equal
B) Resistance is cancelled
C) The circuit radiates all its energy in the form of radio waves
D) Inductive reactance and capacitive reactance cancel
notes.choicesExplained: A: equal current and voltage values are not what defines resonance. B: resonance cancels reactance, not resistance. C: a resonant LC circuit stores energy in its fields, it does not radiate it all away.
notes.explanation: At resonance, XL and XC are equal and opposite, so they cancel and leave only resistance to oppose current.

notes.front: How do inductive and capacitive reactance each change as frequency rises?
notes.back: Inductive reactance (XL) rises with frequency; capacitive reactance (XC) falls with frequency.
notes.explanation: Swap these and you will pick the wrong choice on any frequency-behaviour question.

notes.front: How are impedance and admittance related?
notes.back: Admittance is the reciprocal of impedance: high impedance means low admittance, and vice versa.
notes.explanation: They describe the same AC circuit from opposite directions, opposition versus ease of current flow.
